<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Plan 009 shipped chunked embeddings and predicted this residual (impl-guide risk #2): estimate_tokens() is bytes/3, so content denser than ~2.55 chars/token — punctuation-heavy code, tool dumps, base64 — sits under the ~7,500-token window unsplit and the provider rejects it: `400 Invalid 'input[0]': maximum input length is 8192 tokens`. A retry re-sends the same bytes, so it fails forever. MEASURED IN PROD 2026-09-01/02: five embed jobs state=failed attempts=3 terminal=false — four `embed:git:github.com/AI-Substrate/pij:raw:…`, one `embed:conv:recovery:raw:c5a6be2d…` (a CONVERSATION turn). Largest observed item 20,872 chars → bytes/3 says ~6,957 tokens, real >8,192. A peer government (harness-engineering) is holding a ~250-seat conversation backfill until this lands, because every oversize turn in it would land silently in the same failed bucket. HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY FIRST (not a fact): crates/core/src/tokens.rs already defines FILL=(2,3) so fit_to_cap effectively assumes 2 bytes/token, but 009's chunk_plan() (crates/daemon/src/enrich.rs) appears to size its window from estimate_tokens (3 bytes/token) without the FILL margin — if so, 20,872 chars would have been split by the margin alone, and aligning the window is the cheap half of the fix. The self-heal is the half that survives content denser than any constant.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A provider cap rejection never becomes a permanent failure for a splittable input: the offending item is identified, re-split tighter, and re-issued, bounded by a fixed number of rounds.
- When the bound is exhausted, the job fails with a message naming the item, its byte length, and the ratio reached — never a bare provider echo.
- chunk_plan's window honours the same FILL margin as fit_to_cap, so the common dense case never reaches the heal path; the chunk-count cost of that alignment is MEASURED on the fixture corpus and reported, not guessed.
- The five jobs stuck in prod complete (or fail with a named reason) after deploy, with before/after evidence read from `flowspace3 status` and the jobs table.
- Search over previously-failed content works: a turn from the recovered conversation job is findable by `flowspace3 search`.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No tokenizer dependency (option b of row 117) — the module's own rationale for an estimate stands.
- No change to TOKEN_BUDGET, batch sizing, or the sub-batching f-001 added, beyond what re-issuing a re-split item needs.
- No CLI changes; no conversation-ingest changes; nothing in crates/cli.
- No change to the 8192 cap constants or the provider adapters' wire shapes — only their error CLASSIFICATION (cap-rejection must be distinguishable from other 400s).
